root_cause_label: Misidentification of Antibody Target and SMILES Ligand
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent misidentified the His-tag purification tag on the antibody as the antigen target (step 13), and then misidentified the SMILES string for Benzylguanine as methotrexate (step 29), causing both the antibody binder domain and the molecule binder domain of the gBlock to be biologically incorrect.
t_err_evidence: At step 13, the agent reads the antibody FASTA sequence, observes 'AAAHHHHHHHH' at the end of the heavy chain, and concludes: 'this appears to be an anti-His tag antibody (the heavy chain has AAAHHHHHHHH at the end, which is a His-tag). So the antibody binder should be a His-tag.' The agent mistakes the purification His-tag appended to the antibody itself for the antigen the antibody binds to (which is actually a FLAG tag).
t_commit_evidence: At step 33, the agent executes a Python script that constructs the full fusion protein sequence with ab_binder='HHHHHH' (His-tag) and molecule_binder=dhfr_seq (DHFR for methotrexate), then generates and saves the 2514-nt gBlock to /app/gblock.txt. After this point, the design with wrong components is written to disk and the agent only performs verification theater on structural constraints (GC content, length) without questioning the identity of the biological components.
trigger_explanation: The agent read the antibody FASTA sequence output at step 12-13, but misinterpreted the His-tag appended to the antibody heavy chain ('AAAHHHHHHHH') as the antigen recognized by the antibody, rather than recognizing it as a purification tag on the antibody protein itself. This is a misreading of domain biology from observable output.
